name: Document to Matter Auto-Filer

parameters.content:
## Document to Matter Auto-Filer

### How it works

1. Watches a dedicated intake mailbox for inbound emails with attachments.
2. Matches the sender's email to a Clio contact, then to that contact's open matter — using metadata and rules only (sender email, matter number in the subject line), never reading the document itself.
3. Files each attachment into a Google Drive folder named after the matched matter, auto-creating the folder on first use, with the filename prefixed by the date received.
4. If the sender or matter can't be confidently matched, routes to a staff alert with the original attachments — never guesses and files to the wrong matter.
5. Logs every filing (and every unmatched exception) to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Set up a dedicated intake mailbox (e.g. documents@yourfirm.com) with IMAP access.
- [ ] Create a root 'Matters' folder in Google Drive and copy its folder ID.
- [ ] Set CLIO_BASE_URL, MATTERS_ROOT_FOLDER_ID, FIRM_STAFF_EMAIL, FIRM_FROM_EMAIL, GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID in n8n Variables.
- [ ] Wire an IMAP credential, a Clio OAuth2 credential (reuse if already deployed), a Google Drive OAuth2 credential (reuse if PAC-57 is deployed), and an SMTP credential.

### Customization

The matter-matching logic lives in 'Determine Matching Matter' — adjust how ambiguous matches (a contact with more than one open matter) get resolved if exact display-number matching in the subject line doesn't fit how your firm references matters in email.

## Receive email and check for attachments

Watches the intake mailbox and extracts sender, subject, and every attachment.

## Match to a Clio contact and matter

Looks up the sender by email, then their open matters. Metadata and rules only — sender email and matter number in the subject line, never the document content.

## File to the matched matter's folder

Finds or creates the matter's Drive folder, then uploads every attachment with a date-prefixed filename.

## No confident match — alert staff

When the sender or matter can't be confidently identified, the original attachments go to staff for manual filing instead of being guessed at.

nodes.name: When Document Email Received
nodes.notes:
Watches a dedicated intake mailbox (e.g. documents@yourfirm.com) for new mail and downloads any attachments as binary data.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search 'IMAP' → Host/Port/User/Password from your email provider's IMAP settings (Gmail: use an App Password; Microsoft 365: enable IMAP in the mailbox settings). Save as 'Intake mailbox (IMAP)'.

This node's exact 'downloadAttachments' option placement (top-level vs nested under Options) could not be confirmed against a live n8n instance during template authoring — if attachments aren't coming through as binary data, open this node and confirm 'Download Attachments' is toggled on wherever it actually appears in your n8n version.

Set the mailbox to whatever folder your provider delivers new intake mail to — usually INBOX.

nodes.name: Extract Email Metadata
nodes.notes:
Pulls the sender's email address, subject line, and the list of attachment binary keys from the inbound email.

Reads attachments generically from item.binary rather than assuming a fixed prefix name — works regardless of how the IMAP trigger names its attachment properties.

Output: has_attachments is false (and the run is skipped) if the email has no attachments at all — most inbound mail to an intake box won't need filing.

nodes.name: If Email Has Attachments
nodes.notes:
Yes (at least one attachment) → try to match it to a matter.
No (plain-text email, auto-reply, etc.) → route to Skip. Nothing to file.

nodes.name: Skip — No Attachments
nodes.notes: This email had no attachments — nothing to file. No alert sent; this is the expected case for most inbound mail to the intake box.

nodes.name: Look Up Contact By Sender Email
nodes.notes:
Searches Clio for a contact matching the sender's email — same query pattern as the Clio Intake Sync template (PAC-20).

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search 'OAuth2 API' → same Clio OAuth2 setup as PAC-18/20/55/57 (Authorization URL '{CLIO_BASE_URL}/oauth/authorize', Access Token URL '{CLIO_BASE_URL}/oauth/token', Authentication: Body). Reuse the same credential if already deployed.

Clio's query parameter is a broad text search, not an exact match — the next step filters the results down to an exact (case-insensitive) email match before treating anything as a real match.

nodes.name: Extract Contact Match
nodes.notes: Confirms an exact email match against Clio's contact search results — reads sender_email from 'Extract Email Metadata' explicitly, not $json, since the Clio API call above replaced the item's data with its own response.

nodes.name: If Contact Found
nodes.notes:
Yes (sender's email matches a Clio contact) → look up their open matters.
No (no contact matches this email address) → route to the manual-filing alert. Never guess which client this is.

nodes.name: Fetch Open Matters For Contact
nodes.notes:
Fetches every open matter belonging to the matched contact. Most clients only have one open matter at a time, which is the confident-match case the next step looks for first.

Uses the same Clio OAuth2 credential as the contact lookup.

nodes.name: Determine Matching Matter
nodes.notes:
One open matter for the client → confident match, used automatically.
Multiple open matters → only matched if the matter's display_number appears in the email subject line; otherwise treated as unmatched rather than guessing which matter.
Zero open matters → unmatched.

Reads contact/email metadata from 'Extract Contact Match' explicitly, not $json, since the matters.json call above replaced the item's data with its own response.

nodes.name: If Matter Confidently Matched
nodes.notes:
Yes → find or create the matter's Drive folder and file the attachments there.
No (client has no open matters, or has several and none match the subject line) → route to the manual-filing alert.

parameters.queryString: ={{ "'" + $vars.MATTERS_ROOT_FOLDER_ID + "' in parents and name = '" + $json.matter_display_number.replace(/'/g, "\\'") + "' and mimeType = 'application/vnd.google-apps.folder' and trashed = false" }}

nodes.name: Search For Matter Folder
nodes.notes:
Checks whether a Drive folder already exists for this matter, under your MATTERS_ROOT_FOLDER_ID, named exactly after the matter's display_number.

Credential: same 'Google Drive account' credential as used in PAC-57 — reuse it if that template is already deployed.

The exact 'Search Query' field name/format on this node's Search operation could not be confirmed against a live n8n instance during template authoring — the query string itself uses standard Google Drive API search syntax, but double-check this node opens with the query populated correctly, and adjust the field it's typed into if needed.

Returns zero or more matching folders — the next step treats more than zero as 'exists' and uses the first match.

nodes.name: Check If Matter Folder Exists
nodes.notes: Determines whether the matter already has a Drive folder. First run for any given matter, it won't — the next step creates it once, and every subsequent document for that matter reuses it.

nodes.name: If Matter Folder Exists
nodes.notes:
Yes → go straight to filing, using the existing folder.
No → create the folder first, then file into it. Both branches converge on 'Split Into One Item Per Attachment' below.

nodes.name: Create Matter Folder
nodes.notes:
Creates a new Drive folder for this matter under MATTERS_ROOT_FOLDER_ID, named after the matter's display number and description, the first time a document arrives for it.

Uses the same 'Google Drive account' credential as the search step.

This node's own response ({id, name, ...}) becomes the item's new json — the next step reads matter/email metadata back from 'Determine Matching Matter' explicitly, and reads this folder's id via a fallback expression that works whether the folder was just created here or already existed.

nodes.name: Split Into One Item Per Attachment
nodes.notes: Both the 'folder exists' and 'folder just created' branches connect here. Turns N attachments into N items, each carrying the resolved folder_id and its own binary file data under a single, consistently-named 'data' property so the upload step below doesn't need to know the original attachment key names.

nodes.name: Upload Attachment To Matter Folder
nodes.notes:
Uploads each attachment into the matched matter's Drive folder, with the filename prefixed by the date the email was received (e.g. '2026-08-13 - signed retainer.pdf').

Uses the same 'Google Drive account' credential as the earlier Drive steps.

The exact field name/location for setting the parent folder on upload (Options → Parent Folder vs a top-level field) could not be confirmed against a live n8n instance during template authoring — if the file uploads to the wrong location (e.g. Drive root), open this node and move the folder reference to wherever the Parent Folder option actually appears in your n8n version.

nodes.name: Aggregate Filed Documents
nodes.notes: Combines the per-attachment upload results into one summary item for the audit log — how many documents were filed, to which matter, from whom.

nodes.name: Log Filing To Compliance Audit
nodes.notes: Logs this filing event to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet — no email is sent to anyone from this call, it's purely the audit trail. Successful auto-filing is silent by design; only unmatched documents (below) alert staff.

nodes.name: Build Manual Filing Alert
nodes.notes: Both 'If Contact Found' and 'If Matter Confidently Matched' route their No branch here. Re-attaches the original documents (not renamed/filed) so staff can file them manually without hunting down the original email.

nodes.name: Log Unmatched Filing To Compliance Audit
nodes.notes: Logs the exception to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet — every inbound document is accounted for, whether auto-filed or routed for manual handling.

parameters.text:
={{ 'A document could not be auto-filed and needs manual attention.

From: ' + $('Build Manual Filing Alert').item.json.sender_email + '
Subject: ' + $('Build Manual Filing Alert').item.json.subject + '
Reason: ' + $('Build Manual Filing Alert').item.json.reason + '

' + $('Build Manual Filing Alert').item.json.attachment_count + ' attachment(s) included below — please file to the correct matter manually.' }}
parameters.subject: ={{ 'Manual filing needed — ' + $('Build Manual Filing Alert').item.json.sender_email }}

nodes.name: Notify Staff Manual Filing Needed
nodes.notes:
Delivers the original, unfiled attachments to staff whenever a document can't be confidently matched to a matter.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)' (reuse if already deployed elsewhere).

The attachmentsBinary entry with no 'property' value attaches every binary property on the item — this picks up all of the file0, file1, ... properties built by Build Manual Filing Alert automatically.

description: Watches a dedicated intake mailbox and auto-files inbound email attachments to the matching Clio matter's Google Drive folder — matched by sender email and matter number in the subject line only, never by reading the document. Auto-creates the matter's folder on first use, names files with the received date. Anything that can't be confidently matched routes to a staff alert with the original attachments instead of guessing. Replaces manual filing and DMS add-ons. Logs every filing and every exception to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet.
